items.title: Continuous Control for Meta Ray-Ban Displays
items.summary: I led sensor fusion, gesture algorithm development, evaluation, and iterative improvement of two continuous control gestures for MRBD. I also contributed to their integration in the product firmware and OS. Wrist turn is a core gesture enabling always-available volume control and contextual zoom control. Wrist move is an advanced gesture for scrolling and 2D pointing. Both gestures combine EMG and IMU sensing on the Meta Neural Band.

items.title: Multimodal Perception for AR and VR
items.summary: I worked on multiple projects to improve multimodal perception across Meta Reality Labs's device portfolio. This research answered several questions about how to effectively combine gaze (eye tracking) and hand tracking, EMG handwriting with microgestures, head tracking with touchpad gestures, and more. The resulting algorithms and study insights have been integrated into Orion AR and Meta VR Glasses and are shaping future product directions.

items.title: Next-generation EMG Continuous Control
items.summary: I worked closely with EMG sensing teams at Meta to explore, influence, and evaluate next-generation continuous control schemes for AI and AR glasses. Some of this work has been published in Nature and efforts to improve gesture robustness and expressiveness continue. Stay tuned for future product announcements from Meta!

items.title: Understanding and Improving 3D Sketching
items.summary: This multi-year project forms the core of my PhD research. It started with a set of studies characterizing mid-air 3D sketching. We then developed SymbiosisSketch, a hybrid tablet+AR tool for expressive 3D sketching. Finally, we built Mimicry, a novel algorithm for sketching curves on surfaces in VR. The first two papers have inspired many follow-up works in the HCI and graphics communities, and a Mimicry-like algorithm was later integrated into the surface sketching tool in Gravity Sketch.

items.title: 3D Sketch Creation and Automatic Surface-Fitting
items.summary: This project, led by Emilie Yu, produced two creative tools for creating 3D sketches and surfacing them. The first is an interactive tool called CASSIE for creating 3D sketches from scratch in VR and automatically surfacing them. The second is an offline algorithm for fitting high-quality piecewise-smooth surfaces to 3D sketches created using CASSIE, other VR tools, or desktop tools for 3D sketching.

items.title: 3D Hand Gestures for Animation Authoring
items.summary: In collaboration with Adobe Research, I elicited hand gestures for VR animation authoring and then built a gesture recognition system for animation authoring. The system supports performance-based and keyframed animation of rigid objects and demonstration of dynamic phenomena using particle systems.

items.title: Volumetric Truss Topology Optimization
items.summary: In this project, I collaborated with researchers at Adobe, MIT, and Reichman University to develop a new algorithm for generating volumetric Michell trusses. These trusses result in a lightweight structure for a given load and boundary conditions, and can be parametrically edited using industry-standard tools such as Autodesk Fusion. In addition to a technical paper and a poster presentation, this work was also exhibited at University of Toronto's Robarts Library.

items.title: Design Exploration from Concept Sketches
items.summary: As part of my Master's thesis at IIT-Kanpur and Inria, I developed a system for exploring design variations by interpolating between multiple concept sketches. Concept sketches are early-stage design sketches that are rough and incomplete, which makes the interpolation task challenging.
